content:
Avery Johnson: Feedback from 2 demos this week: people keep getting stuck on the word “Optimize”. They assume it’s (a) a separate SKU, or (b) some auto-magic model training thing. The convo derails into “what exactly is Optimize?” vs the story we want (cost/latency levers + observability).

Avery Johnson: When I say “Redwood Optimize” out loud, I get: “so do you change the model weights?” :facepalm:

Hannah Schmitt: +1. Same in EMEA. They hear “Optimize” and think “consulting” or “fine-tuning service”. Then procurement asks if it’s an add-on.

Priyom Das: Also sometimes sounds like a generic feature name. People want to know what we actually *do* (batching/caching/quantization recs + regression alerts).

Soojin Lee: This is super helpful. Agree the label is causing confusion.

Soojin Lee: Suggestion for talk track: lead with outcome language, not the module name.

Soojin Lee: Instead of “Optimize”, try: “Cost & performance controls” or “Production economics toolkit” (and then in small text: “Redwood Optimize”).

Camila Reyes: Yeah—“Optimize” reads like a black box. “Production economics” is our positioning anyway. We can say: “We give you knobs + guardrails to reduce $/token without breaking quality.”

Markus Klein: From SE side: I’d rather not hide the product name entirely (people will see it in Console), but we can frame it as a set of capabilities.

Markus Klein: Maybe: “Optimization (batching + caching + routing policies)” instead of just “Optimize”.

Soojin Lee: Totally. Proposed phrasing for live demo transition:

Soojin Lee: “Now that we’ve got a working endpoint, the real question is: what does it cost at scale, and how do we control that? Redwood has cost & latency controls built into the runtime + Console—batching, caching, and routing—plus recommendations and regression alerts.”

Avery Johnson: That’s much better. “Cost & latency controls” is the phrase I’ve been searching for.

Alex Martinez: +1. In the SDK examples we can mirror that language too (e.g., `batching=true` becomes “enable batching (cost control)” in comments).

Elliot Price: For the internal guide + talk track doc, I can swap section headers:
- “Optimize” -> “Cost & performance (production economics)”
- keep “Redwood Optimize” as the Console label callout

Camila Reyes: If we’re updating slides: can we change the slide title to “Lower $/token without sacrificing latency” and only mention “Optimize” in the subheader?

Soojin Lee: Yes. Also recommend we avoid “recommendations” as the lead verb (sounds like vague AI). Better: “configuration suggestions backed by measurements + evals.”

Priyom Das: Question: do we want to say “unit economics” or is that too CFO-y for a technical audience?

Soojin Lee: Use “unit cost” / “$/1M tokens” for engineers; “unit economics” for exec/procurement if needed. In the standard 30-min talk track, I’d keep it “cost per token” + “latency SLO”.

Markus Klein: One more: customers ask “is this automatic?” We should be explicit: “We can auto-suggest configs, but you control policies and can A/B + rollback.”

Soojin Lee: Great point. Add line: “No black box. You can pin versions, canary changes, and roll back.”

Avery Johnson: Awesome. Can we get an approved “one-liner” I can use verbatim?

Soojin Lee: Draft one-liner:
“Redwood’s production economics toolkit helps you lower cost per token with explicit controls like batching, caching, and quantization—plus observability and eval-based alerts so you don’t trade away quality or reliability.”

Avery Johnson: :thumbsup: That’s it.

Camila Reyes: I’ll update the deck copy (v1.0 -> v1.1) with:
- Slide header: “Production economics: cost & latency controls”
- Subheader: “Redwood Optimize (in Console)”

Elliot Price: I’ll patch the internal talk track doc with the new transition + the “not a black box” clarification and drop a link here when published.

Markus Klein: Works for me. For the live steps, we can label the section in the run-of-show as “Cost/latency controls” so SEs don’t say “Optimize” as the first word.

Soojin Lee: Action items:
- Camila: update deck titles/subheaders
- Elliot: update talk track script
- Markus: update run-of-show section labels

Soojin Lee: We’ll keep the UI name as-is for now, but talk track should lead with outcomes. If we still see confusion after 2 weeks, we can raise a product naming/UI label change with Dylan/Console team.

Hannah Schmitt: Love it. This should make the flow smoother.

Avery Johnson: Thanks all. I’ll test the new phrasing on my next call and report back.
